questions.q: What is science, and how is it different from technology?
answer: Science is a systematic way of studying the natural world through observation, questioning and experiment. It grows out of curiosity — the urge to ask what, why and how about the things around us.

answer.text: It builds reliable knowledge about nature, from why the sky is blue to how plants make food, by testing ideas against evidence.
Technology applies that knowledge to solve practical problems and make useful tools — medicines, vehicles, phones and machines.
The two are closely related: science provides understanding, and technology puts it to work. Advances in one often drive the other.

questions.q: Describe the main steps of the scientific method.
answer: The scientific method is the careful, step-by-step way in which scientists investigate a question.

answer.text: It begins with observing something in nature and asking a clear question about it.
The scientist makes a reasonable guess, called a hypothesis, that might answer the question.
The guess is tested through experiments, and the results are carefully measured and recorded.
The results are analysed to see whether they support the hypothesis, and a conclusion is drawn. Tests are repeated to be sure.

answer: Throughout, science relies on evidence rather than opinion.

questions.q: What are the main branches of science?
answer: Science is a vast subject, and to study it more easily it is divided into several main branches.

answer.text: Physics studies matter, energy and the forces of nature, explaining things like motion, light, heat, sound, electricity and magnetism.
Chemistry studies the materials that make up the world, what they are made of, their properties, and how they change and combine with one another.
Biology is the study of living things, both plants and animals, including how they live, grow and interact with their surroundings.
There are also branches such as astronomy, the study of the sky and heavenly bodies, and geology, the study of the Earth, along with many others.

answer: Thus science is divided into branches like physics, chemistry and biology, each studying a different part of the natural world.

questions.q: How is science a part of our everyday life?

answer.text: Science is not only found in laboratories; it is present in everything we do. The food we cook, the clothes we wear, the way we travel and the medicines we take all involve science.

Cooking uses heat and changes in materials, a mirror uses the reflection of light, a fan and a fridge use electricity, and a bicycle uses forces and motion. Doctors, farmers, engineers and cooks all use science in their work.
Science also helps us understand natural events such as rain, day and night, and why the seasons change, and it teaches us to observe, question and find answers.

answer: Thus science is woven into daily life, helping us do our work, use tools and understand the world around us.
